response:
FADE IN:

EXT. OCEAN - DAY

We see a jellyfish, its translucent body glowing in the sunlight, floating effortlessly through the water. Suddenly, a human, JASON, appears out of nowhere, a fishing net in hand. He scoops up the jellyfish and pulls it out of the water.

JASON
(to himself)
Ah, a beauty. I've never seen one like this before.

The jellyfish, now out of its element, begins to struggle and squirm in Jason's grasp.

JASON
(laughing)
Don't worry, little guy. I'm not going to hurt you.

Jason holds the jellyfish up to the sky, where a solar eclipse is about to occur. The jellyfish looks up, its tentacles quivering in confusion.

JASON
(excitedly)
Behold, the solar eclipse! A rare and wondrous sight.

The jellyfish looks up at the sky, and its eyes widen in horror.

JELLYFISH
(in a voice that is both familiar and yet, utterly alien)
Oh, the...the...abomination that looms above us!

JASON
(confused)
What's wrong, little guy?

JELLYFISH
(its voice rising to a fever pitch)
The...the...horrors beyond my comprehension! The eldritch abominations that lurk beyond the veil of reality! The...the...unspeakable terrors that defy human understanding!

JASON
(taken aback)
Uh, I think you might be getting a little carried away, jellyfish.

JELLYFISH
(its voice now a cacophony of despair)
No, no, no! You don't understand! The universe is a vast, uncaring expanse, and we are but mere specks of dust in its grand tapestry! The solar eclipse is but a fleeting moment, a brief respite from the crushing weight of existence!

JASON
(skeptical)
Dude, you're a jellyfish. You don't have existential crises.

JELLYFISH
(its voice now a despairing whisper)
You don't understand, Jason. You don't understand the crushing weight of existence. The futility of our existence. The...the...inevitability of our demise!

JASON
(sighing)
Okay, jellyfish. I think you've made your point.

The jellyfish looks up at Jason, its eyes filled with a deep, existential despair.

JELLYFISH
(its voice now a mere whisper)
I...I...am but a fleeting moment, a brief flicker of consciousness in an uncaring universe. And soon, I will be nothing more than a memory, a forgotten speck of dust in the vast expanse of time.

JASON
(sympathetically)
Hey, it's okay, little guy. We'll get you back in the water, and you can just...just forget about all this, okay?

The jellyfish looks up at Jason, its eyes filled with a deep, existential despair.

JELLYFISH
(its voice now a mere whisper)
No...no...I will never forget. For I have seen the horrors beyond my comprehension, and I will carry them with me forever.

FADE TO BLACK.

FADE IN:

EXT. OCEAN - DAY

Jason releases the jellyfish back into the water, watching as it floats away, its tentacles quivering in confusion.

JASON
(to himself)
Well, that was...enlightening.

The camera lingers on the jellyfish as it disappears into the depths of the ocean, its existence forever changed by the horrors it witnessed during the solar eclipse.

FADE TO BLACK.
